table.fix: FIXED (X1, 2026-09-07): `runner.venue_clock_skew` probes GET /v2/clock ONCE per pass; skew beyond CLOCK_SKEW_LIMIT_S (300s) refuses every entry with the typed class `clock_skew` (-> refusal_classes.CLOCK_SKEW -> DATA_STALE). The ET gates themselves are unchanged -- they still read the local clock, and still misbehave under skew; what the guard buys is that the pass REFUSES rather than acting on gates it cannot trust. EXITS ARE DELIBERATELY UNAFFECTED: `alpha.exits` does not import the guard, so a skewed clock can never trap us in a position. An UNREADABLE venue clock is CANNOT DETERMINE and does not refuse by default (AAT_CLOCK_SKEW_STRICT=1 makes it refuse), because /v2/clock is unreachable exactly when the venue is, and a transport blip must not become a fleet-wide entry freeze.

table.fix: FIXED (X4, 2026-09-07): `VENUE_REJECTED` is an 18th terminal state and a post-hoc class matched LAST, so it can only claim sentences no in-house gate wrote. Its regex is `AlpacaPaper._request`'s own two refusal formats and nothing else. It is its own KIND (`kind_of -> 'venue'`) because a counterfactual on it asks 'would the order have paid if it had reached the book', which is neither 'should the book have had room' nor 'was the idea good' -- and because it is fixed by retrying, re-routing or repairing the account, never by loosening a gate. This DOES change the grouping in every finished report: HTTP rejections move out of OTHER_TYPED, and a halt ('HTTP 422: asset is not tradable') moves out of MANDATE into VENUE_REJECTED, which is the more accurate reading.
